utterances.text: That day you are talking about is 19th April 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was on 19th April 1993. I will remember that date for the rest of my life, for three reasons. The first reason is that the shelling took place which we all will remember, and we had a lot of injured civilians who were our patients. That date is also the birthday of my son, so that is the second reason why I remember it. On that day, my daughter was supposed to go and congratulate my son on his birthday and she was to cross that square. She met some friends and colleagues about 50 yards from the place where this shell fell and she was held up for a while by this conversation, otherwise she would have been probably dead. So this is the third reason why I remember this event. On that day, we received many patients severely injured. There were 18 of them who were severely injured and there were 38 with lighter injuries. There were 15 who were killed. One of the 18 of the seriously injured was brought to me. His name is Velimir Sekerovic; he had serious neck injuries. He was hit in the front of the neck by the shrapnel and practically his pharynx, the throat, was almost gone, and the larynx was exposed. He was still alive after the aspiration and after we cleaned the wound. We put him on the respirator and then proceeded to perform the surgery. He has no larynx left now, so he is a seriously disabled person. Since he had also some burns, he also has very large scars, so that he has problems in turning his head, so this is the patient that I personally treated in the surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, you at the time of the shelling on 19th April 1993 were not the director of the hospital, were you? You took that position later on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I later came to that position of the Director and at that time I was the head of the Crisis Staff which was concerned solely with the organisation of these extraordinary events that were taking place at that time, and also I was a specialist for ear, nose and throat at that time, at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you noted, doctor, that you yourself did some work on one of the injured civilians, but you drew a distinction between slight injuries, of which you noted there were approximately 38, and serious injuries, of which there were 18. Could you tell the court how you made the distinction between slight and serious injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a general rule for ascertaining the degree of an injury, whether it is a serious or slighter. Slighter would be any minor injury, that is that does not affect any systemic injuries, where we do not expect injuries that would stay, and we believe that these patients can go back home without durable damage, whereas the serious injuries are the ones where one of the major cavities of the body would be open, whether it was cranial or abdominal or other; also if there are multiple injuries to the system, one or more bodily systems, or if any of the bone structures have been damaged, or maybe a very large injury to the skin, like higher degree burns. Some of the functions are later expected to be impaired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Doctor, as Director of the Hospital, you were asked by the Office of the Prosecutor to compile the records of the 18 individuals that suffered serious injury as a result of the shelling on 18th April 1993, and you have compiled a list of those in the document before you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President and your Honours, the document that is the list prepared by Dr. Beganovic is the next exhibit, exhibit 220. The document you have before you is the document that you prepared of the 18 that were seriously injured; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: While you did not treat all these patients, did you as the Director of the Hospital have a chance to review the medical files of these 18 individuals prior to coming into the court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I treated the patient under number 4, Velimir Sekerovic. I personally treated him, I treated that wound and I already mentioned it, and I checked the files of the rest of them, that is the release papers and the case histories, and all these patients were identified as serious injuries, with extremities that had to be amputated or with some of the bodily cavities being open.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These 18 were the ones that suffered serious injury as a result of the shelling that took place on 19th April 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. These were all injuries sustained through explosive device.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you could, doctor, could you go down the list and, referring to the files that are beside you, could you refer to the case histories for each of these individuals, could you tell us if they are male or female, the approximate date of birth and could you tell us the serious injuries each particular patient suffered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have this document. If I have understood things correctly, the third column perhaps is the date of birth; at least this is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is fine, Mr. President. I would like the doctor to tell us exactly what the serious injuries are here. Some of them are amputations. Some of them are as radical as amputations; some are not as radical as amputations. Nevertheless, with regard to the particular count which reflects the suffering sustained by the civilians, I think it is beneficial for the court to understand exactly what these individuals suffered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do as you like, of course, but I think according to the indictment, what is important is to make the connection between the injuries and the shelling, about which the witness already said they were serious, unless that is contested by the Defence. We do not have to take the medical file of each of the individuals. Does the Defence challenge any of this? The doctor has just said there were 18 serious injuries, very serious injuries. He explained what constituted the serious injury. I do not know, does the Defence want any additional explanations. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I do not think there is any aspect of the good doctor's testimony that the Defence will contest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I hope that the witness understands why I have intervened here. We are not asking for explanations about every piece of this testimony, but what I think is important in the accusations against General Blaskic is to show the connection between these injuries and the shelling. This document has the date of 18th April 1993, about which the witness is testifying. He said that what had happened were serious injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this particular witness is not the witness that is there to make the connection. This witness is just a witness to explain to the court what exactly the serious injuries are. I think that the witness can go through these 18 patients rather quickly and then we will be just completing the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let the witness say what he needs to say, but I want you to understand my objection! A witness is here to testify and he has just done so; he said there were injuries that were serious. Now, of course, we can be satisfied with that sentence -- I do not want to waste time because of me, but the judges could also ask that the exhibit medical files -- that the 18 medical files be given to us, which would be difficult for you. The witness has taken an oath; he says what he saw, he was the head of the Crisis Staff. He said that, as a doctor, these 18 people who came in on that day, because they had been injured in the shelling and that they were seriously injured. That is all I have to say. Now do as you like and let the witness say what he has to say the, but we are counting the minutes and every minute counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Could you go through those files, doctor, and tell us briefly the serious injuries suffered by the 18 patients which are depicted in the report that you filed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I shall try and be very brief going through this list. Number 1, is Biljana Francic, born in 1967, and she had an injury in the area of the abdomen, and shell fragments remained inside, so a cavity had to be opened and this fits within the description I gave of a grave bodily injury. Number 2, Zehrudin Valentic, born in 1970. He also had a serious explosive injury of the chest. Then number 3 is Goran Ilic, born in 1973, who also sustained explosive injuries in the neck, the chest and abdomen, which also required surgery and opening a bodily cavity. Number 4 is Sekerovic Velimir. I have already referred to him; it was a grave injury of the neck which I personally operated on. Then number 5 is Mario Jurcevic born 1971 in Zenica, and he had an injury of the lower jaw; a part of it was missing when he was admitted. Then also he had a wound in the neck and a part of the upper jaw as well. Number 5 is Ahmet Mutapcic, born in 1938 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that is number 6, doctor, on your list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 6 is Ahmed Mutapcic, again an explosive injury in the lower jaw, a highly complex fracture, and an injury of the head. Number 7 is Jasmin Hodzic. He also had an explosive wound in the area of the head, in the upper jaw, and his face and the temporal region, which affected his ear. His ear was injured, and the large arteries, the temporalis artery on the left-hand side with heavy bleeding. So number 8 is Muratovic Ibrahim, an explosive wound in his extremities, both his lower legs and his left upper arm with the bones being shattered of the left upper arm, and the right upper leg. Number 9 is Cvjetinovic Velibor, born in 1968. He had to have an amputation of his foot, of his left foot, and an injury of the right foot as well. His big toe on his right foot had to be amputated and a bone from the foot removed, the right foot, the metatarsal bone, and an explosive wound in the left shoulder. Then there is Suada Kadric, born in 1956, Kadric. She had an explosive wound in the lower leg and the hip, left lower leg and hip, with many shell fragments in the right hip. Muhamed Zelenkic, born in 1961, and in his case there was an explosive wound on the left upper leg, and a fracture of the bone, a complicated fracture of the left. Then Zekira Muratovic, born in 1957, also explosive injuries in the left foot and left lower leg, with the absence of the first and second metatarsal bones, which means partial amputation of the foot. Slobodan Vukovic, born in 1966. In the case of this patient, there was also an injury caused by explosives in the left shoulder, a fracture of the left upper arm, a multiple fracture of the left upper arm and multiple rib fracture, ribs 1 to 3, which means an injury of the chest as well. 14 is Numo Pojskic, born in 1914. He also had an injury of the ribcage on the left, an injury of the abdomen and shell fragments in both areas. That was Pojskic. Then we come to Muradif Dedic, born in 1948, again an explosive injury with an amputation of his left lower leg and a complicated fracture of the left upper leg and a complex wound in the left upper leg, because the shrapnel went upwards. Then we have Muharem Colak, born in 1977. He had a very serious trauma of the left lower leg due to which he suffered a bleeding and traumatic shock. Then Ivan Loncar, born in 1931 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me doctor, starting with Colak Muharem, was his left leg amputated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muharem Colak?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Born in 1977, he had a pressure wound and a wound caused by explosive of the left lower leg, and heavy bleeding and shock. (Not interpreted) heavy bleeding and shock and amputation of his right lower leg. The last patient is Asim Osmanagic, born in 1947 from Zenica. He also had a very large explosive wound in the right upper leg and he suffered a haemorrhagic shock, and he was primarily treated for this shock due to heavy bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we finish with those, doctor, if we could go back to Loncar Ivan where the right leg was amputated. I believe the English interpretation did not come through, Mr. President, and I believe that the patient Loncar had his right leg amputated up to the knee. Can you just give that medical file result again, please, doctor, so we can make sure the record is complete? It should be the second to last one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivan Loncar. What are you interested about him? He had traumatic amputation, traumatic amputation because of the explosion of his extremity of his right leg, and he suffered haemorrhagic shock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are not going to go into the medical records of the 38 that are slightly injured. We are just leaving it at the 18 and the death certificates of the approximately 15 will be addressed by the other witness. At this time, we would offer exhibit 220 into evidence and we have no further questions of Dr. Beganovic. Thank you, doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo? I see that your client is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a moment please, your Honours. Mr. President, the Defence has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Riad, Judge Shahabuddeen? I have no questions either. We could interpret and speak a great deal about all of this. Were there any forensic tests done? I am not asking this of the witness but of the Prosecutor. Were any forensic reports done, because in count 8, you speak about serious injuries? Were there any forensic tests that were done?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There will be some other witnesses that will discuss what actually happened directly after the shelling. The only reason, Mr. President, as I said at the outset that we brought Dr. Beganovic in out of order was so that Dr. Beganovic could get back to the hospital in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, you answered my question. I would like to thank you on behalf of my colleagues and the entire Tribunal, doctor, for having come here. I suppose you have a great many responsibilities as the head of the hospital and treating those patients who were so seriously injured in the war. We would like to thank you and hope that he can go back peacefully to his work. Can we have Dr. Beganovic escorted out of the courtroom. Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, before you have the next witness brought in, where are we now? According to the list which you gave to us, there were anonymous witnesses. I would like to see where we are. You had said that there would be 13 witnesses. What is the schedule that you have in mind? How many have already testified? According to the Registrar, we have already heard five.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have six more witnesses for this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. So then you will finish by the end of this week; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. All right, we can have the next witness brought in. Is this a protected witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the next witness also is a protected witness. He will have a pseudonym and he will have face distortion. He will be referred to as Witness V, is that correct, as in victoire?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, this is Witness V.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In summary, Mr. President, my colleague Mr. Kehoe has identified the areas that apply to the Zenica shelling. This also is a Zenica shelling witness, so his testimony will relate to count 1, persecution, paragraph 6.1, paragraph 6.2; counts 2 to 4, unlawful attacks on civilians and civilian objects, paragraph 8; and counts 5 through 10, the wilful killing and causing of serious injury, paragraph 9. In summary, Mr. President and your Honours and counsel, Witness V is a photographer who has lived in Zenica most of his life. He will testify about the locations where various artillery shells fell on 19th April 1993. He responded to the scene, he took a number of photographs which he will identify and we will introduce into evidence, and he will also identify a video film which accurately depicts the scene of the shelling. That concludes my summary, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. A relatively brief witness? About how long will you be working with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think that he has to identify approximately 15 photographs, which he will describe to the Trial Chamber and there is a video film that should last about 11 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. All right, Registrar, let us have Witness V brought in, please. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness V, first of all, do you hear me? First we want you to check your identity, your name on this piece of paper, but do not state your name, do not say it out loud. Just make sure this is in fact who you are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You will now read the declaration which is being given to you. This is your oath, in your own language. Read it, please. WITNESS V (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are a witness for whom protective measures have been put into place. We will call you Witness V. You will testify about all the points that the Prosecutor has mentioned to us, specifically what you experienced at the time of this shelling of Zenica on 19th April 1993. The Prosecutor will ask you several questions. After that, you will testify in your own words and the Prosecutor will ask for certain clarifications in support of his indictment against General Blaskic who is being tried before this court. The floor is yours, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness V, are you a freelance photographer and were you so employed on 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you present in the city of Zenica on 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you hear detonations coming from part of the town of Zenica on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have the assistance of the usher in showing the witness a series of photographs, approximately 16 photographs which will be part of an exhibit. Mr. President, your Honours and counsel, it will be Prosecutor's exhibit 221. For your Honours' benefit, counsel's benefit and anybody in the viewing audience, the photographs that will be seen and presented by the Prosecutor in part of this case will be extremely graphic and the video film which will conclude the presentation of the evidence will likewise be extremely graphic and disturbing, so I inform your Honours of that at this point in time. Please, Mr. Usher, if you could disassemble that exhibit and take the first photograph and place that on the ELMO? Mr. President and your Honours, this for the record should be 221/1. Witness V, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell the judges what this photograph represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the view from my house in the direction of the area where the shells fell. I started to take pictures because that is my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you shortly thereafter go to that location where the smoke was coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Usher, I am going to interrupt with one other exhibit. Could I have exhibit 222, please? Could that be placed on the ELMO? Witness V, first of all can you describe the area where this smoke or the shelling had occurred? Can you give us a description of that area, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The smoke can be seen rising from this area marked with C. That was where a vehicle caught fire from the shell, a shell set it on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness V, what kind of an area was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the very centre of town, where there are many pedestrians, housewives, people with nothing to do, students, pensioners. That is how towns were designed in our country, with a downtown area where everything took place. It was mostly the commercial centre of the town. That is also where the cafe-bars and restaurants are and free space for sitting down, walking around and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now in a moment I am going to be showing you a series of photographs. You have drawn this particular diagram, have you not, diagram 222?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You indicated with various letters, A through E, the locations where you took particular photographs that I am going to show you in a few minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Let me begin -- thank you, Mr. Usher, I have concluded with this particular exhibit. Let me begin then by turning to the area on the diagram with a letter A, and show you two exhibits. The first exhibit will be 221/2; if that could be placed on the ELMO. Do you recognise that photograph, Witness V?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was that photograph taken at the position marked letter A on diagram 222?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What does that photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The place where the shell impacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could turn to the next photograph, 221/3, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was that also taken in and around the area of location A?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very close to it, to area A, and this is one of the consequences of the shelling. These were kiosks selling hot dogs, food. It is very nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let me turn to point B which is marked on your diagram that you drew for us. Let me start with photograph 221/4. Did you take this photograph and does this photograph accurately depict the scene of the shelling on 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you please tell the judges what this particular photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see the spot where the second shell impacted, and the effects the shrapnel has had on the car. This is the point of impact of the shell, that is point B.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This shows a number of dead people in and around that particular point of impact; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let us turn to another photograph, 221/5, which is another view of the same scene.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same car, but from a slightly different angle, and you can see the victims in the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to the next photograph, 221/6. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph shows the victims. This is about 15 or 20 metres from points A and B where the shells fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Could you point out with your pointer the number of people who are dead and who appear in that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So starting at the left-hand side, there appear to be two bodies and then in the middle there appears to be a body.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are other photographs where you can see more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next photograph if we can, 221/7. Can you describe that photograph? Is that a similar photograph taken at the same scene, point B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A little to the right, taken from a position slightly to the right in relation to the previous photograph and you can see the victims. They are mostly around this wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There are some other photographs we can show later that better depict that. Now can we turn to the location on the diagram which is indicated point C, and could we have the next photograph, 221/8. Witness V, is this a photograph taken from the location of point C and can you tell the court what it depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the car that was on fire and of which fire I saw the smoke and started towards the place where the shells fell and the vehicle burnt out as a result of these shells and these shop windows were also broken. The crater was here, the crater and the traces of the shell fragments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The crater is indicated on the left-hand side of that photograph near the margin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if we turn to 221/9 a slightly different view, does this better show the crater and the car that is damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness V. Let me turn to the next photograph, which is 221/10. This is a series of four photographs that shows the main street and the pedestrian mall from slightly different views. Let us start with 221/10. What does that particular photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is directly across from the points A and B where the shells fell. The injured had already been taken away and the dead were still lying on the ground. Had I come a bit earlier, I would have probably seen the injured ones as well, but the civilian protection personnel had already brought them, taken them to the hospital, so originally there were more victims there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the large building in the centre of that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the main department store, and in front of the department store was a plaza where people sat and took rest, and where the victims are lying on the ground. That is where the stalls were, where the vendors were selling cigarettes and such items, but that is where people would stroll and this is where you pass from one part of the town to the next, and this was in the -- around midday and the mosque is nearby, it is right there, and at the time when the shells were fired, people would go to the mosque and also the housewives would be shopping and also students would be on a midday break, people who would meet and get together there, so that is where the life was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Approximately how many metres away from this location was the mosque located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 50 metres from the dead. Very close to the department store.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn to the next exhibit which should be 221/11, which is a slightly different view. Can you describe what this particular view shows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the view from the centre of town towards another part of town, in the direction where the street goes. You can see the kiosks, the victims, and you can see where the points of impact were and also the burnt-out car. This was point B and point A is right outside of the picture, and you can see the consequences, thereby I mean the victims. Had it not been for the vehicles there probably would have been more victims. They were parked there so I think that saved some lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next photograph, 221/12, another photograph which you took. Does this show three of the victims of the shelling, one in the upper top left-hand corner and one in the centre and one in the left lower foreground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and this is directly across from the points A and B, and so this was the consequence of these shells, these victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if we can turn to the last photograph in this series, which is 221/13, can you tell us what this particular photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This photograph shows that there were stalls there for vendors. You can see that people would walk there, that this was a pedestrian area, and also it depicts the victims, and you can see some of the traces, because some people had been carried off the scene. This is what I found. This is also directly across from points A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let me turn to location D on your diagram, which is exhibit 222, and turn to the first photograph from that area, which is 221/14. First of all, before you identify this particular photograph, can you describe what kind of an area this was to the judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a pedestrian street and this was lined up with coffee bars and coffee-shops, where the youth would gather, and this is where the shell hit and the coffee bar was downstairs and upstairs, and there is another photograph which has the view from the other side, so there is no car traffic here, only pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For the record, that particular photograph you just pointed to -- I seem to have lost my computer monitor transmission -- there we go. In the photograph, there is a building with a hole right in the building. The hole in the building in the centre; is that where the shell impacted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the point of impact of this shell, where it hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let me turn to 221/15. Can you tell the judges again what this photograph is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the same street, but you can just see how many coffee-shops and coffee bars there are, how many tables out. Across from it is the independent TV station in Zenica, right there (indicates). The shell impacts here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Lastly let me turn to point E on your diagram and the last photograph in this series. This is photograph 221/16. Can you tell the judges what this photograph shows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here you can see a bus stop, you can see where the shell impacted and I will also point where the local radio station is. This is the point of impact of the shell, this is the bus stop and this is the radio station where you can see the traces of the shell fragments (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Witness V, did you have an opportunity to see a videotape with me last night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That videotape is in three sections; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The first section shows the general area where the shells in the pedestrian mall and the area where the department store are located; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The second part of the film shows a burning car, which would be near your point C in your diagram; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the third portion of the film shows an area of the coffee bars where the shell impacted above the coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You were at those locations on 19th April 1993. Does the film accurately depict the scene as you saw it and as you remember it on 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Dubuisson, this film is in three segments. It is interrupted, the first segment, by a small blue field that will appear and then there is a second brief segment of about 20 seconds and then there is a blue field and then there is a third longer segment of approximately 6 minutes. I defer to you how you care to identify that, whether as exhibit 223 as a total exhibit or as 223/1 to 223/3. I leave that to your discretion. However I would again, Mr. President and counsel and those people in the audience who would be watching this film, inform you that this film is extremely graphic and disturbing. With that, Mr. President, I would ask the booth to lower the lights and play the whole film in one sequence. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a staircase where you go down into the supermarket section of the department store. These are the points A and B where the shells impacted. These are the consequences of the shells. This is directly across from points A and B. This is down the street, this is across and here you can see the consequences. There would have been more victims, but the first shell that fell killed the people that it did, and then after that the people fled. Otherwise, it is a very dense area, there are a lot of pedestrians there. There were other dead there, but I encountered fewer of them than a colleague of mine who arrived before me, and took pictures of more of them. So this is in front of the department store called Bevrecenka, right across points A and B where the shells fell. Those were the stalls for vendors and it was their merchandise. There are also passers-by and pedestrians. These are body parts. There was also a children's playground nearby and a large residential block and you could also see the mosque on the other side, the department store, and also the area where there are a lot of coffee-shops and coffee bars where the youth gathered. Up there was the movie theatre and the plaza, and then again the staircase going into the basement of the department store. This is point C where the car was burning. These are the consequences of what was marked as D, where the coffee bars are and where the independent television called Zetel was located. This is the coffee shop marked with D. Above the door is the impact of the shell. This was a coffee bar and both downstairs and upstairs. That is the point marked as D. This is again the consequence of this and the wounded had already been taken away. This is the inside of the coffee bar, and again this is where the shell marked with D impacted. What you can see out of the window is the independent television, Zetel. A lot of youth gathers here. You can also see the power of the explosion in these images. This is a vehicle that belongs to the independent television station. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could have the lights, please, thank you. Thank you, Witness V. Mr. President, I would move for admission of Prosecutor's exhibits 221 through 223 and then I have concluded my examination of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. May I turn to the Defence, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Just a few questions. Good evening, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Witness V, did you take any other photographs than what we saw here tonight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know the judicial bodies and the police and the others did not really allow us to take pictures. I sometimes had to behave like a paparazzi, I had to lie or I had to dissemble, so there were others. As you see, there were no police or representatives of judicial bodies there, so as soon as we arrived we had to -- we were lucky to have taken this many, otherwise there would have been many more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I did not understand. Do you have any other photographs than the ones that you offered to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have any more. There was also a shortage of photographic materials and they would not let me work afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you point me to the direction of the north here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Maybe we can put on the map. This is exhibit number 222 of the Prosecution. Can you point in this diagram, number 222, where the north was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The west was here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please just the north, that is the standard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me see, north would be this way (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you put your pointer in the direction of north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my very lay orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So in which direction is north going, let us say from point D?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let us see. From point D going towards B but not quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us see, from point D diagonally across towards B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but this is a very lay type of orientation, so I would probably take it with some reservation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There are no other questions. Witness V, the Tribunal thanks you for your testimony, which demonstrated a great deal of courage, the fact that you went down into the midst of all of this and took these very striking pictures. We will have you escorted out of the courtroom now. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes our witnesses for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We will suspend the hearing now. Let the witness leave. We will meet together tomorrow at 10.15. The court stands adjourned. (6.30 pm)

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.15 am the following day)
